key_insight: TREX automates the end-to-end LLM fine-tuning lifecycle by coordinating a Researcher agent (design & search) and an Executor agent (data, training, eval) using a tree-based exploration strategy to systematically explore and refine training choices.
problem_solved: Manual LLM fine-tuning is time-consuming, error-prone, and fragmented across literature review, dataset curation, experiment design, hyperparameter search, and orchestration; TREX addresses the lack of an end-to-end automated system for these tasks.
method: Agent-based architecture: a Researcher agent formulates requirements, generates candidate experiments and hypotheses while an Executor agent runs data collection, training, and evaluations.
Tree-based exploration: organize the design space as a branching tree of configurations and decisions to systematically explore, prune, and refine promising paths.
Iterative feedback loop: automated evaluation signals guide the Researcher to propose refinements, enabling automated experiment selection, reproducibility, and pipeline orchestration.
impact: TREX can drastically reduce human effort and cycle time for LLM fine-tuning, making experimentation more systematic, reproducible, and scalable for practitioners and researchers.
visual_elements: System diagram showing two core agents (Researcher ↔ Executor) and their interactions
Tree-structured exploration graph that visualizes branching experiment configurations and pruning
End-to-end pipeline timeline from requirement analysis → data & literature research → experiment run → evaluation → refinement
Before/after comparison (e.g., effort or time saved) or a flow of automated decisions vs. manual steps (icons for automation)
paper_title: TREX: Automating LLM Fine-tuning via Agent-Driven Tree-based Exploration
paper_authors: Zerun Ma, Guoqiang Wang, Xinchen Xie, Yicheng Chen, He Du
